title: First-run boot and install screens misbehave - splash never shows, install screen strobes
description:
Pre-existing and cross-platform - the user reports the splash always fails on the first run, not only on Linux. Surfaced in the MPI-407 Linux verification log: main.js:751 logs "Splash failed to load: ERR_FAILED (-2)" for app/splash/splash.html, which IS present in the artifact, so this is not a packaging miss - Electron rejects a pending loadFile with ERR_FAILED when the WebContents is destroyed mid-navigation (a missing file would be ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND -6). The behaviour is inverted against the splash purpose stated at main.js:722, "visible instantly, gate the main window": it fails on the slow run it exists to cover and loads fine on the warm run where nothing needs covering. Two candidate causes, neither settled - the main window ready-to-show firing on Chromium network error page and closing the splash at main.js:419-421, or the splash own load being starved (~8.4s from creation to rejection). Reproduce before fixing; a warm-cache run cannot test it. Deliberately NOT fixed inside 1.3.0 - main.js is baked into verified artifacts and a cosmetic splash does not justify a new SHA plus re-verifying six bundles.

MERGED 2026-08-01: this card absorbs MPI-412 (Engine install screen strobes between 'preparing dependencies' and the download progress).
- MPI-412 - cosmetic, seen live on the Linux engine install 2026-07-30, candidate causes unverified.
WHY ONE CARD: Both are first-run-only visual defects on the boot into install path, both are cosmetic (nothing fails), and both are reproduced by the same act: a cold first launch that goes on to install an engine. One investigation session covers the pair.
The absorbed card(s) are closed as done/rejected - not built, kept as the record - and their full original text stays on disk at tasks/<id>/.
